problem: Several summation signs have no limits, so students cannot tell whether the sum runs over all n or only a range: "x[n] = Σk x[k] δ[n − k]" in Section 1 and "s[n] = Σk=−∞n h[k]" in Section 3. In the second one the upper limit n is not raised, so it reads like multiplication.
fix: Write x[n] = Σ<sub>k=−∞</sub><sup>∞</sup> x[k] δ[n − k] and s[n] = Σ<sub>k=−∞</sub><sup>n</sup> h[k].

where: Worked example 1 (steps 7–8) and quiz Q4, Q8
problem: Exponents are not marked, so (0.5)nu[n], (0.9)n, ejωn, H(ejω) and e−jω can be read as plain multiplication by n. In step 7 this makes h[n] look like 0.5·n·u[n], which diverges, contradicting the stability answer in step 8.
fix: Use raised exponents everywhere: h[n] = (0.5)<sup>n</sup>u[n], (0.9)<sup>n</sup>, e<sup>jωn</sup>, H(e<sup>jω</sup>), e<sup>−jω</sup>.

problem: The answer lists only the sums y[1] = 1 + 2 = 3 and y[2] = 1 + 2 = 3. The two terms are not identified, so a student cannot see which product comes from which index and cannot check the working.
The chapter defines H(ejω) without saying when this sum converges. Students may plug in h[n] = u[n] and conclude the frequency response exists, though that system is not BIBO stable.
fix: Add one sentence: the frequency response exists when Σ |h[n]| is finite, that is, for every BIBO-stable system; an unstable system such as h[n] = u[n] has no finite H(ejω).
